extracted.intended_audience: publishers, journalists, complainants, and members of the public interested in Australian media standards
extracted.subtask_description: High-level statement of the Australian Press Council's standards, principles and complaint-handling procedures that are binding on member publications (print and online) and guidance for complainants and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote high standards of media practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The council is responsible for promoting high standards of media practice, community access to information of public interest, and freedom of expression through the media
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the core responsibility/mission of the Council and frames its work and standards-setting activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements of Principles (binding)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council's Statements of Principles are binding on all publications which are subject to its jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Statements of Principles serve as enforceable standards for publications under the Council's jurisdiction; they are foundational to the Council's standards framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of General Principles as part of Standards of Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Press Council's Statement of General Principles forms part of its Standards of Practice which are binding on all print and online publishers that are members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that the general principles are incorporated into the Standards of Practice and apply to both print and online member publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Guidelines (the Press Council's Statement of General Principles forms part of its Standards of Practice which are binding on all print and online publishers that are members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory guidelines accompany the Standards of Practice to provide guidance to publications; the page groups these with the Standards and Principles as part of the Council's normative materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints: information and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Information for complainants; What can be complained about; Who can complain; How to make a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council provides specific information for complainants covering scope (what can be complained about), eligibility (who can complain), and procedure (how to make a complaint). The site also directs users to the fastest route: the online complaints form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of complaints: investigation, mediation and adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Council processes for investigation, mediation and adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint handling is described as a process that may include investigation, mediation and formal adjudication; these are the procedural stages the Council uses when dealing with complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy work: statements, submissions and charter promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Australian Press Council makes statements and submissions on a range of public policy issues within its areas of interest. The Council encourages other organisations to adopt its Charter for a Free Press Australia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council issues public policy statements and submissions and promotes broader adoption of its Charter; it also publishes other materials such as media comment, research reports, issues papers and summaries of consultations.
